questions.question: The Union Government introduced a major overhaul of labour laws, consolidating twenty-nine existing regulations into four new codes effective from which of the following dates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21 November 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Government** of **India** has consolidated **29 existing central labour laws** into **four comprehensive Labour Codes** to simplify and modernize the regulatory framework for the workforce.
 
• These reforms are scheduled to be fully effective from **21 November 2025**, establishing a unified commencement date for the new legal regime across the country.
 
• The overhaul aims to improve the **Ease of Doing Business** in **India** while ensuring better **social security** and **working conditions** for over **50 crore workers** in both the organized and unorganized sectors.
 
• The **Ministry of Labour and Employment** spearheaded this initiative to replace archaic laws, some of which date back to the **1920s** and **1940s**, with a more contemporary legislative structure.
 
• As **Labour** is a subject under the **Concurrent List** (List III) of the **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**, both the **Central Government** and **State Governments** have the authority to draft rules under these codes. ***Hence, the correct answer is 21 November 2025.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Four Labour Codes:**
 
 
• **Code on Wages, 2019:** This was the first code to be passed by **Parliament** in **August 2019**. It replaces four major acts: the **Minimum Wages Act, 1948**, the **Payment of Wages Act, 1936**, the **Payment of Bonus Act, 1965**, and the **Equal Remuneration Act, 1976**. It introduces a **National Floor Level Minimum Wage** to be set by the **Central Government**.
 
• **Industrial Relations Code, 2020:** It consolidates laws relating to **Trade Unions**, conditions of employment, and settlement of industrial disputes. Notably, it increases the worker threshold for requiring government permission before **retrenchment** or **closure** from **100** to **300 workers**.
 
• **Social Security Code, 2020:** This code integrates nine laws, including the **Employees’ Provident Fund Act** and the **Maternity Benefit Act**. For the first time, it provides a legal framework for **social security** for **gig workers** and **platform workers**.
 
• **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020:** It streamlines 13 laws related to the health and safety of workers. It mandates **annual health check-ups** for certain categories of employees and simplifies the **registration** process for establishments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact on Wages:** The new codes introduce a uniform definition of **"wages"** across all four legislations. This change is expected to impact **take-home pay** and **provident fund (PF)** contributions, as allowances are now capped at **50%** of the total salary.
 
• **Digitalization:** The government has promoted the **Shram Suvidha Portal** to facilitate **online registration**, filing of returns, and **transparent inspections**, reducing the **Inspector Raj** system.
 
• **Fixed-Term Employment:** The codes provide for **Fixed Term Employment (FTE)**, allowing companies to hire workers for a specific duration with the same **statutory benefits** as permanent employees, thereby increasing **labor flexibility**.
 
• **Gender Equality:** The codes mandate that **women** are entitled to work in all types of establishments, including at **night** (with their consent and safety measures), and prohibit **gender-based discrimination** in wages for the same work.

questions.question: In November 2025, which legislation was highlighted for merging nine Social Security Acts, covering gig and platform workers, and strengthening women-centric provisions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Code on Social Security, 2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Code on Social Security, 2020** is a landmark legislation that aims to extend social security to all employees and workers in both the **organized and unorganized sectors**.
 
• It consolidates and replaces **nine central labor laws**, including the **Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952**, the **Maternity Benefit Act, 1961**, and the **Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972**.
 
• A significant feature of this Code is the inclusion of **gig workers** and **platform workers** under the ambit of social security schemes for the first time in **India**.
 
• The Code empowers the **Central Government** to set up a **Social Security Fund** to provide death and disability cover, health and maternity benefits, and old age protection for unorganized workers.
 
• It strengthens **women-centric provisions** by ensuring **maternity benefits** and allowing women to work in all establishments at **night** (between **7 PM and 6 AM**) subject to their consent and safety conditions provided by the employer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Code on Wages, 2019**:
 
 
• This Code was the first of the four labor codes to be passed. It amalgamates **four acts**: the Payment of Wages Act, Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Bonus Act, and Equal Remuneration Act.
 
• It aims to universalize the provisions of **minimum wages** and timely payment of wages to all employees, irrespective of the sector and wage ceiling.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Relations Code, 2020**:
 
 
• This Code merges **three laws**: the Trade Unions Act, 1926; the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946; and the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
 
• It introduces the concept of **fixed-term employment** and seeks to streamline dispute resolution and labor relations in **industrial establishments**.
 
 
 
• **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020**:
 
 
• It consolidates **13 central labor laws** relating to the safety, health, and working conditions of workers.
 
• It applies to establishments with **10 or more workers** and includes specific provisions for **inter-state migrant workers** and **audio-visual workers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gig Workers and Platform Workers**: Under the **2020 Code**, a **gig worker** is defined as a person who performs work or participates in a work arrangement and earns from such activities outside of the traditional employer-employee relationship.
 
• **e-Shram Portal**: The **Ministry of Labour and Employment** launched this portal in **2021** to create a national database of **unorganized workers** (including migrants and gig workers) to facilitate the delivery of social security benefits.
 
• **Maternity Benefit Enhancements**: While the core entitlement remains **26 weeks** of paid leave (as per the **2017 amendment** integrated into the Code), the new Code ensures broader compliance and easier access for women across various sectors.
 
• **Gratuity Eligibility**: The Code reduces the eligibility period for **gratuity** for certain classes of employees, particularly those in **fixed-term employment**, where it is paid on a **pro-rata basis** even if the five-year service requirement is not met.

• By supporting **11 languages**, Sarvam AI aims to bridge the **digital divide** and foster **digital inclusion** across various states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indic AI Ecosystem:**
 
 
• The development of models in **11 languages** is a significant milestone for **Indic AI**, as most global models primarily focus on Western languages.
 
• **Data Diversity:** The training involves massive **Indic datasets** to capture regional accents and dialects accurately.
 
• **Use Cases:** These models are being applied in sectors like **customer service (IVR)**, **education (audiobooks)**, **banking**, and **government service delivery**.
 
• **Strategic Importance:** Strengthening domestic AI capabilities reduces reliance on foreign tech giants and ensures **data privacy** within national borders under the **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act** framework.

questions.question: In 2025, which state in India is concerned about the invasive species Ruellia Elegans?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Ruellia elegans**, commonly known as the **Brazilian Petunia** or **Red Ruellia**, has emerged as a significant ecological concern in the state of **Assam** in **2025**. • It is classified as an **Invasive Alien Species (IAS)** that has begun to spread rapidly across the **forest floors** and **protected areas** of the state, competing with indigenous flora. • While originally introduced to **India** as an **ornamental plant** due to its vibrant **red flowers**, it has escaped cultivation and established itself in the wild, particularly in the moist and fertile regions of **North-East India**. • The concern in **2025** stems from observations by **botanists** and **environmentalists** that the plant is displacing native ground-cover species, which serves as a critical food source for local **herbivores**. • The rapid proliferation of **Ruellia elegans** is particularly alarming for the **biodiversity hotspots** in **Assam**, where maintaining the balance of native ecosystems is vital for endangered wildlife.

questions.question: In March 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) granted Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) an additional how many years from financial year 2025 to amortise the additional expenditure arising from the revision in pensions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **March 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** issued a notification regarding the financial management of **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**.
 
• The **RBI** granted an additional **five years**, starting from the **financial year 2024-25**, to **amortise** the additional expenditure arising from the **revision in pensions**.
 
• This decision was taken to mitigate the sudden **financial burden** on the **Balance Sheets** of RRBs, which could otherwise lead to a sharp decline in their **profitability** and **capital adequacy**.
 
• The **amortisation** provision allows these banks to spread the total pension liability cost over a period of **five years** in equal installments, rather than charging the entire amount to the **Profit and Loss account** in a single year.
 
• The move follows representations made by the RRB sector regarding the high cost of implementing **pension parity** with **Nationalised Banks**, a requirement mandated by legal and administrative rulings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs):**
 
 
• RRBs were established under the provisions of an Ordinance passed in **September 1975** and the **RRB Act, 1976**.
 
• They were created based on the recommendations of the **Narasimham Working Group** to provide **banking** and **credit facilities** for **agriculture** and other rural sectors.
 
• The **equity** of an RRB is held by the **Central Government (50%)**, the **Sponsor Bank (35%)**, and the **State Government (15%)**.
 
 
 
• **Amortisation in Banking:**
 
 
• In accounting, **amortisation** refers to the practice of spreading an **intangible asset's** cost or a **large liability** over its useful life or a specific period.
 
• For RRBs, amortising pension costs helps maintain a stable **Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR)**, ensuring they meet **regulatory requirements**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• While the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** sets the **monetary policy** and broad **prudential norms**, **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)** is responsible for the **supervision** and inspection of RRBs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pension Parity Issue:** The demand for equal pension benefits for RRB employees compared to their counterparts in **Public Sector Banks (PSBs)** was a long-standing issue, eventually settled by the **Supreme Court of India** in **2018**.
 
• **Financial Impact:** The total **liability** for pension revisions is substantial for many RRBs, especially those with a high number of **retirees** and limited **operating profits**.
 
• **Disclosure Norms:** Banks opting for this **amortisation** are required to make full **disclosure** of the unamortised amount in the **'Notes to Accounts'** section of their **Annual Financial Statements**.
 
• **FY 2025 Significance:** The permission to start the **five-year** window from **FY 2024-25** provides immediate relief to banks preparing their **year-end** audits for the **March 2025** closing.
</ul

questions.question: In August 2025, which of the following countries temporarily closed the Dardanelles Strait to maritime traffic following major forest fires in the Çanakkale province?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turkey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August**, the **Government of Turkey** suspended maritime traffic in the **Dardanelles Strait** due to intense **forest fires** raging in the **Çanakkale** province.
 
• The **Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure** of **Turkey** announced the temporary closure to facilitate **firefighting aircraft** and helicopters to safely scoop water from the strait to combat the blazes. ***Hence, the statement regarding Turkey's involvement is correct.***
 
• The **forest fires** in **Çanakkale** were driven by high temperatures, low humidity, and strong winds, which are common during the **summer season** in the **Mediterranean** region.
 
• The **Dardanelles**, a vital waterway for **global trade**, connects the **Aegean Sea** to the **Sea of Marmara** and serves as a primary route for **oil** and **grain** tankers coming from the **Black Sea**.
 
• Authorities evacuated several **villages** and **universities** in the vicinity of **Çanakkale** to ensure the safety of the residents as the fire spread toward the city center.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geography of the Dardanelles Strait:**
 
 
• The **Dardanelles**, historically known as the **Hellespont**, is a narrow, natural strait located in **northwestern Turkey**.
 
• It forms part of the continental boundary between **Europe** and **Asia**, separating the **Gallipoli** peninsula in Europe from the **Biga** peninsula in Asia.
 
• The strait is approximately **61 kilometers** (38 miles) long and varies in width from **1.2 to 6.5 kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **The Turkish Straits and International Law:**
 
 
• The **Turkish Straits** comprise the **Dardanelles**, the **Sea of Marmara**, and the **Bosphorus** strait.
 
• Transit through these waters is governed by the **Montreux Convention** Regarding the Regime of the Straits, signed in **1936**.
 
• This **international agreement** grants **Turkey** control over the straits and regulates the passage of **naval warships** while guaranteeing the free passage of **civilian vessels** in peacetime.
 
 
 
• **Strategic and Economic Importance:**
 
 
• It is one of the world's busiest **maritime chokepoints**, providing the only access for **Black Sea** nations (like **Ukraine** and **Russia**) to reach the **Mediterranean Sea** and world markets.
 
• Major commodities transported through the strait include **crude oil**, **petroleum products**, **iron**, **steel**, and **agricultural products**.
 
 
 
• **Çanakkale Province:**
 
 
• **Çanakkale** is a major port city and province in **Turkey**, famous for the **Gallipoli Campaign** of **World War I** and the ancient city of **Troy**.
 
• The province is susceptible to **wildfires** due to its dense **pine forests** and the prevailing **meltem winds** during the **summer months**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Impact:** Forest fires in this region lead to significant loss of **biodiversity** and contribute to **carbon emissions**, exacerbating **climate change** concerns in the **Eastern Mediterranean**.
 
• **Infrastructure:** The **1915 Çanakkale Bridge**, which opened in **2022**, spans the **Dardanelles Strait** and is the **longest suspension bridge** in the world, providing a land alternative to the ferry services.
 
• **Emergency Response:** **Turkey** utilizes a fleet of **Be-200** amphibious aircraft and **T-70** helicopters for **aerial firefighting** operations during such crises.

67:T

questions.question: As per the April 2025 monthly Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) data, what was India’s unemployment rate in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5.1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the monthly data released for **April 2025** by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, India’s **unemployment rate** stood at **5.1%**.
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** is the primary source of these statistics, designed to estimate key employment and unemployment indicators at more frequent intervals.
 
• The rate of **5.1%** represents the percentage of persons **unemployed** among the persons in the **labour force** during the specific reference period of **April 2025**.
 
• This data is collected under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, which oversees the collection and dissemination of socio-economic data in India.
 
• The **unemployment rate** is calculated based on the **Current Weekly Status (CWS)**, which provides a short-term snapshot of the labour market's performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**
 
 
• Launched in **April 2017** by the **NSO**, the **PLFS** was established to provide more frequent data on the Indian labour market compared to the previous quinquennial surveys.
 
• It aims to estimate employment indicators in the **short time interval** of three months for **urban areas** only in the **CWS** and annually for both **rural and urban** areas.
 
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**
 
 
• **LFPR** is defined as the percentage of persons in the **labour force** (working or seeking work) in the total population. It helps in understanding the **size of the workforce** available in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Worker Population Ratio (WPR):**
 
 
• The **WPR** is the percentage of **employed persons** in the total population. This indicator is a direct measure of the **level of employment** in the country.
 
 
 
• **Current Weekly Status (CWS):**
 
 
• In this approach, the activity status of a person is determined based on a reference period of the **last 7 days** preceding the date of the **survey**. A person is considered **employed** if they worked for at least **one hour** on any day during the reference week.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Methodology:** The **NSO** uses a **rotational panel sampling** design in urban areas to ensure that the data reflects changes in the labour market accurately over time.
 
• **Significance:** Monitoring the **unemployment rate** monthly or quarterly allows the **Government of India** to tailor economic policies and **social security schemes** to address job shortages or sectoral declines.
 
• **Historical Context:** Before the introduction of **PLFS**, the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** conducted large-scale surveys every **five years**, which often resulted in a time lag for policy intervention.
 
• **Economic Impact:** An **unemployment rate** of **5.1%** in **April 2025** serves as a benchmark for comparing the growth of the **industrial** and **service sectors** against the increasing **population** and workforce entry.

questions.question: Which event was scheduled for 27 June 2025, regarding the DR Congo–Rwanda agreement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deployment of peacekeepers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The scheduled event for **27 June 2025** is the **Deployment of peacekeepers** as part of the implementation phase of the **DR Congo–Rwanda agreement**.
 
• This deployment is intended to stabilize the volatile **Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo**, particularly in the **North Kivu** province, where fighting has been intense between the **FARDC** (Congolese army) and the **M23 rebel group**.
 
• The agreement represents a critical milestone in the **Luanda Process**, a diplomatic effort mediated by **Angola** to mend the fractured relationship between **Kinshasa** and **Kigali**.
 
• The peacekeepers are tasked with supervising the **disengagement of forces** and ensuring that a **buffer zone** is maintained to prevent direct military confrontations between the two nations' proxies or armies.
 
• This specific date was set during high-level diplomatic sessions held in **2024** and early **2025** to provide a concrete timeline for transitioning from a fragile **ceasefire** to a monitored security arrangement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geopolitical Context:**
 
 
• The **Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)** has long accused **Rwanda** of providing military support to the **M23 (March 23 Movement)**, a claim supported by reports from the **United Nations Group of Experts**.
 
• Conversely, **Rwanda** has raised security concerns regarding the presence of the **FDLR (Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda)**, an ethnic Hutu rebel group operating within the **DRC** territory.
 
 
 
• **The Luanda and Nairobi Processes:**
 
 
• The **Luanda Process**, led by Angolan President **João Lourenço**, focuses on the interstate relationship between **DRC** and **Rwanda**.
 
• The **Nairobi Process**, facilitated by the **East African Community (EAC)**, primarily addresses the internal dialogue between the **DRC government** and various local armed groups.
 
 
 
• **Regional Peacekeeping Forces:**
 
 
• The **Southern African Development Community (SADC)** deployed a mission known as **SAMIDRC** in **December 2023** to support the **DRC** government.
 
• The **United Nations** mission, **MONUSCO**, which has been in the country for over **two decades**, began its phased **withdrawal** in **2024**, making the **2025** deployment of new regional peacekeepers vital for filling the security vacuum.
 
 
 
• **Humanitarian Impact:**
 
 
• The conflict in the **Great Lakes region** has resulted in one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with over **7 million** people **internally displaced** within the **DRC** as of **2024**.
 
• The **June 2025** deployment is seen as a prerequisite for the safe **repatriation** of refugees and the delivery of **humanitarian aid** to besieged towns like **Sake** and **Goma**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: As of June 2025, who is the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Omar Abdullah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Omar Abdullah** was sworn in as the first Chief Minister of the **Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir** on **October 16, 2024**, following the first assembly elections held in the region in a decade.
 
• He represents the **Jammu and Kashmir National Conference (JKNC)**, which secured a significant victory in the **2024 Legislative Assembly elections** held in three phases across **September and October 2024**.
 
• As of **June 2025**, he continues to serve as the head of the government, leading a cabinet that aims to address administrative challenges and advocate for the **restoration of statehood** for Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• This election was historic as it was the first since the **abrogation of Article 370** and the reorganization of the state into a Union Territory in **August 2019**.
 
• The **National Conference-Congress alliance** formed the government, with **Omar Abdullah** leading the executive branch after the revocation of **President’s Rule**, which had been in place since **2018**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**:
 
 
• This landmark legislation passed by the **Parliament of India** reconstituted the state of **Jammu and Kashmir** into two separate Union Territories: **Jammu and Kashmir** (with a legislative assembly) and **Ladakh** (without a legislative assembly).
 
• The Act came into effect on **October 31, 2019**, coinciding with the birth anniversary of **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**.
 
 
 
• **Mehbooba Mufti**:
 
 
• She served as the **last Chief Minister** of the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir from **April 2016 to June 2018**.
 
• She is the president of the **Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party (JKPDP)** and was the first woman to hold the office of Chief Minister in the region.
 
 
 
• **Mufti Mohammad Sayeed**:
 
 
• A veteran politician and founder of the **PDP**, he served as the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir twice, from **2002 to 2005** and from **March 2015 until his death in January 2016**.
 
• He also served as the **Union Home Minister of India** from **1989 to 1990**, becoming the first Muslim to hold that specific portfolio.
 
 
 
• **PU Lalduhoma**:
 
 
• He is a prominent politician from Northeast India, currently serving as the **Chief Minister of Mizoram** since **December 2023**.
 
• He leads the **Zoram People's Movement (ZPM)** and is a former **IPS officer** who served in the security detail of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Legislative Assembly**: The current assembly of the Union Territory has a **five-year term**. The number of seats was increased following a **delimitation exercise** completed in **2022**, which allocated **43 seats to Jammu** and **47 seats to the Kashmir Valley**.
 
• **Historical Context**: **Omar Abdullah** previously served as the Chief Minister of the state of Jammu and Kashmir from **2009 to 2014**, making him one of the youngest individuals to hold the post at age **38**.

questions.question: Who flagged off India’s first exported locomotive to Guinea in June 2025?

• The export to the **West African** nation of **Guinea** is part of a strategic vision to enhance India’s footprint in the **Global South** and strengthen bilateral trade relations through infrastructure support.
 
• The flagging-off ceremony highlights the successful implementation of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) mission, where domestic manufacturing units are now capable of meeting international technical standards and specifications.

• **RITES Limited:**

• **RITES** acts as the export arm and provides consultancy services for transport, infrastructure, and related technologies in over **55 countries** across **Africa**, **Asia**, and **Latin America**.

• The shift toward exporting **Diesel** and **Electric** locomotives reflects India's transition from being an importer of railway technology to a net exporter.
 
 
 
• **Global Reach of Indian Railways:**
 
 
• Apart from **Guinea**, India has successfully exported locomotives, coaches, and wagons to countries like **Sri Lanka**, **Bangladesh**, **Myanmar**, **Vietnam**, and **Mozambique**.

questions.question: As per the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, published in June 2025, the number of start-ups rose from 453 in 2016 to 34,293 in 2024. This growth in entrepreneurship primarily supports which Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)?
questions.solution:

• As per the **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report, 2025**, released in **June 2025**, the number of recognized **start-ups** in India saw an exponential rise from **453** in the year **2016** to **34,293** by **2024**.
 
• The growth in **entrepreneurship** is a direct indicator of **Target 8.3** under **SDG 8**, which focuses on promoting development-oriented policies that support productive activities, **job creation**, **innovation**, and the growth of **MSMEs**.
 
• This increase in start-ups reflects India's robust **innovation ecosystem**, which fosters **self-employment** and contributes significantly to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** growth of the nation.
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** tracks these indicators to monitor India’s progress toward the **2030 Global Agenda**.

__
 
• **SDG 1 (No Poverty):** This goal focuses on ending **poverty** in all its forms. It includes targets for **social protection**, access to **basic services**, and supporting those affected by **economic**, social, and environmental shocks.
 
• **SDG 4 (Quality Education):** This objective ensures **inclusive** and equitable quality **education** and promotes **lifelong learning** opportunities. It tracks literacy rates, **school enrollment**, and vocational training availability.
 
• **SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities):** This goal aims to reduce **inequality** within and among countries by improving the regulation of **financial markets**, encouraging **development assistance**, and empowering lower-income earners.
 
• **Startup India Initiative:** Launched on **January 16, 2016**, by the **Government of India**, this flagship initiative was designed to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing **innovation** and driving sustainable **economic growth**.
 
• **NITI Aayog:** In India, **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency responsible for the **SDG India Index**, which evaluates the progress of **States and Union Territories** in achieving the **Global Goals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Impact:** The rise to over **34,000 start-ups** underscores India's position as one of the largest **startup hubs** globally, providing a foundation for **Target 8.2** (achieving higher levels of **economic productivity**).
 
• **National Indicator Framework (NIF):** The **NIF** is the largest monitoring framework for **SDGs** in India, consisting of **300+ indicators** that align with the **Global Indicator Framework**.
 
• **Employment Generation:** Start-ups play a crucial role in providing **decent work** for the **youth**, reducing the **unemployment rate**, which is a key component of **SDG 8** metrics.

In front of a capacity crowd at the **Stade de France**, he not only secured the Olympic title but also set a new **Olympic Record** and **World Record** of **6.25 meters** during the final. ***Hence, the statement regarding his victory is correct.***

• Often referred to as the **“Oscars of Sport,”** these awards were established in **1999** by founding patrons **Daimler** and **Richemont**.
 
• The first ceremony took place on **May 25, 2000**, in **Monte Carlo**, with **Nelson Mandela** delivering a famous speech about how "sport has the power to change the world."
 
• The awards celebrate the most remarkable sporting achievements of the calendar year across multiple categories, including **World Sportswoman of the Year**, **World Team of the Year**, and **World Breakthrough of the Year**.

• He has dominated the **Diamond League** circuit and holds multiple **World Championship** titles (**2022** and **2023**) in addition to his **two Olympic Gold medals** (**Tokyo 2020** and **Paris 2024**).

• **Cristiano Ronaldo**: Though a legend of **Football**, he was not the winner of the **2025** Sportsman category, despite his ongoing record-breaking career in **Saudi Arabia**.
 
• **Usain Bolt**: A **four-time** winner of the Laureus World Sportsman of the Year (**2009, 2010, 2013, 2017**), he remains the most decorated athlete in the history of this specific award.
